title: The Vector Space Model: Visual Guide
outline: Title: The Vector Space Model: Visual Guide

1. From Weights To Axes | a slider over the occurrences of `index` turning the previous lesson's (1 + ln tf) x idf weight into a coordinate on a four-term vocabulary, with the tf = 0 branch showing an empty axis | the weighting scheme produces the number and bag-of-words decides where it goes, so a zero coordinate is not stored at all and idf only pays out on an axis the document activates

2. Building The Vector | steppers over the vocabulary [database, index, query, vector] building a document vector against the fixed query [0, 0, 1, 1], with the dot product expanded term by term | only coordinates nonzero in both vectors contribute, which is exactly what traversing the query terms' postings does, and no shared axis means no lexical score at all

3. Dot Product Versus Cosine | B's second coordinate dragged against fixed q = [1, 1, 0] and A = [2, 1, 0], with a toggle between full cosine and the runtime form that drops the query norm | dot product ranks by magnitude and cosine by direction, so at B = [1, 4, 0] the dot products 3 and 5 reverse into cosines 0.949 and 0.857, and dropping the constant query norm never changes an ordering

4. The Alpha Dial | the exponent alpha dragged from 0 to 1 over two documents sharing numerator 6 with norms 2 and 8, plus a comparator between [3, 0, 0] and [1, 1, 1] | full cosine is one point on a dial rather than a neutral default, and cosine normalizes the vector norm and not the token count, so identical total weight can give norm 3 or norm 1.732

5. Pivoted Length Penalty | the slope s and the collection average length dragged over four documents from a 200-word answer to a 5,000-word manual, showing each denominator and the reordering | pivoted normalization tilts a line around average length, documents at the average always divide by 1, and both too little and too much normalization put the wrong document first
